A row of seven simple coleoptile experiment drawings, each showing a small pale-green coleoptile growing from a little pot of soil, with yellow light arrows coming from the right-hand side in experiments 1 to 6 and no light (darkness shown by a grey background panel) in experiment 7. 1: intact coleoptile bending towards the light. 2: coleoptile with its tip removed, standing straight and short. 3: coleoptile with a black opaque cap on its tip, standing straight. 4: coleoptile with a black opaque sleeve around the part below the tip, bending towards the light. 5: tip removed and replaced on a thin pale-yellow agar block, bending towards the light. 6: a thin grey mica sheet inserted into the shaded left side just below the tip, standing straight. 7: decapitated coleoptile in darkness with a small agar block placed on its left side only, bending to the right. Experiment 6: the thin grey mica sheet stands VERTICALLY (upright, like a thin wall) inserted into the coleoptile from its shaded left side just below the tip, blocking the left half of the stem. Experiment 4: the black sleeve wraps the stem below the tip, and the whole coleoptile bends clearly towards the light. Do not write numbers.

Line graph of the effect of auxin concentration on the growth of roots, buds and stems. The x-axis shows auxin concentration increasing from left to right on a logarithmic scale (no numbers needed, just low to high). The y-axis shows growth response, with a horizontal zero line in the middle: above the line is stimulation, below the line is inhibition. Three bell-shaped curves in three colours: the root curve (brown) peaks at the lowest concentration and falls below zero early; the bud curve (green) peaks at a middle concentration; the stem curve (blue) peaks at the highest concentration, at a point where the root curve is well below zero.
